subproblems.title: Operator vs Hilbert–Schmidt norm, distance to a subspace, and the projection trace identity
subproblems.statement:
(i) For all m, k and every linear map A : R^m → R^k, ‖A‖ <= |A|, where ‖A‖ is the operator norm and |A| = (Σ_i |A e_i|^2)^{1/2} = hsNorm A is the Hilbert–Schmidt norm (e_i the standard basis).
(ii) For every linear subspace T ⊆ R^m and v ∈ R^m, |p_{T⊥} v| = dist(v, T), where p_{T⊥} is the orthogonal projection onto T⊥.
(iii) For linear subspaces P, T ⊆ R^m with dim P = dim T, trace(p_{T⊥} ∘ p_P) = (1/2)|p_P − p_T|^2, where |·|^2 = hsNormSq.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (m k : ℕ) (A : Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k), ‖A‖ ≤ hsNorm A) ∧ (∀ (m : ℕ) (T : Submodule ℝ (Rn m)) (v : Rn m), ‖Tᗮ.starProjection v‖ = Metric.infDist v (T : Set (Rn m))) ∧ ∀ (m : ℕ) (P T : Submodule ℝ (Rn m)), Module.finrank ℝ P = Module.finrank ℝ T → LinearMap.trace ℝ (Rn m) (Tᗮ.starProjection.toLinearMap ∘ₗ P.starProjection.toLinearMap) = hsNormSq (P.starProjection - T.starProjection) / 2

It is applied with m = n + l, since Amb n l is by definition Rn (n + l). Parts (i) and (iii) are not used in this subtree. It is the comparator-accepted declaration of DAG node root.tilt_excess_height_estimate-a1.projection_algebra-a1 (candidate commit 164f08e), already a resolved dependency of this node. Source (as recorded for the accepted node; 'the parent' and 'the supplied proof' in the rest of this text refer to that node's own parent, not to gwe_vertical_first_variation): the supplied proof's facts
- (F3) (Simon 5.2.1 proof, display (2));
- '||A|| <= |A|' (step 5);
- '|x'| = dist(x − ξ, T)' (step 7).

Setting: R^m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m), with orthonormal basis e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1, hsNormSq A = Σ_i ‖A e_i‖^2 and hsNorm A = (hsNormSq A)^{1/2}. Every subspace W of R^m is finite-dimensional, hence complete, so the orthogonal projection p_W := W.starProjection exists. It is self-adjoint and idempotent, with range W and kernel W⊥.

(i) Operator norm <= Hilbert–Schmidt norm.
1. Let v ∈ R^m have coordinates v_i. Then v = Σ_i v_i e_i and ‖v‖^2 = Σ_i v_i^2.
2. By linearity, A v = Σ_i v_i A e_i. The triangle inequality and Cauchy–Schwarz in R^m give
    ‖A v‖ <= Σ_i |v_i| ‖A e_i‖ <= (Σ_i v_i^2)^{1/2} (Σ_i ‖A e_i‖^2)^{1/2} = ‖v‖ · hsNorm A.
3. hsNorm A >= 0, so the operator-norm bound (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound) gives ‖A‖ <= hsNorm A.

(ii) Distance to a subspace.
4. v = p_T v + p_{T⊥} v (Submodule.starProjection_add_starProjection_orthogonal). So ‖p_{T⊥} v‖ = ‖v − p_T v‖ = dist(v, p_T v).
5. Let w ∈ T. Then v − w = (v − p_T v) + (p_T v − w), with v − p_T v ∈ T⊥ and p_T v − w ∈ T. By Pythagoras,
    ‖v − w‖^2 = ‖v − p_T v‖^2 + ‖p_T v − w‖^2 >= ‖v − p_T v‖^2,
  with equality at w = p_T v ∈ T. Hence infDist(v, T) = inf_{w ∈ T} ‖v − w‖ = ‖v − p_T v‖ (Mathlib Submodule.dist_starProjection_eq_infDist).
6. Steps 4 and 5 give ‖p_{T⊥} v‖ = infDist(v, T). This is exactly SimonGMT Chapter04.norm_normalProjection_eq_infDist.

(iii) The trace identity.
7. Write p := p_P, q := p_T and k := dim P = dim T. An orthogonal projection onto W is a projection onto W along W⊥, so its trace is dim W (LinearMap.IsProj.trace; equivalently, in an orthonormal basis adapted to W ⊕ W⊥ its matrix is diag(1,…,1,0,…,0)). So trace p = trace q = k.
8. By step 4 applied to every vector, p_{T⊥} = I − q. Hence
    trace(p_{T⊥} ∘ p) = trace p − trace(q ∘ p) = k − trace(qp).
9. For any linear B on R^m, hsNormSq B = Σ_i ‖B e_i‖^2 = Σ_i ⟨B^*B e_i, e_i⟩ = trace(B^*B). This uses that in an orthonormal basis the trace of C is Σ_i ⟨C e_i, e_i⟩ (the diagonal of its matrix).
10. B := p − q is self-adjoint, and p^2 = p, q^2 = q, so B^*B = (p − q)^2 = p − pq − qp + q. With trace(pq) = trace(qp) (LinearMap.trace_mul_comm),
    hsNormSq(p − q) = trace p + trace q − 2 trace(qp) = 2k − 2 trace(qp).
11. By steps 8 and 10, hsNormSq(p − q)/2 = k − trace(qp) = trace(p_{T⊥} ∘ p_P). In Lean form: LinearMap.trace ℝ (Rn m) (Tᗮ.starProjection.toLinearMap ∘ₗ P.starProjection.toLinearMap) = hsNormSq (P.starProjection − T.starProjection)/2. ∎

subproblems.statement: For all n, l and every linear isometry q of R^(n+l): (i) graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b' = graphPoint (a - a') (b - b') for a, a' in R^n, b, b' in R^l; (ii) |graphPoint a b|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2; (iii) every z in R^(n+l) equals graphPoint a b for some a in R^n, b in R^l; (iv) the orthogonal projection P onto T_0 = rotatedPlane q = q(R^n x {0}) satisfies P(q(graphPoint a b)) = q(graphPoint a 0).

Context. This child supplies the graph-coordinate calculus. gwe_vfv_norm_le_first_block_add_infDist uses parts (i)-(iv): q^{-1}x = graphPoint a b, p_T x = q(graphPoint a 0), p_{T⊥}x = q(graphPoint 0 b) and |x|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2. Source (as recorded for the accepted node; 'the parent' and 'the supplied proof' in the rest of this text refer to that node's own parent, not to gwe_vertical_first_variation): elementary linear algebra for the contract's graphPoint / horizontalPlane / rotatedPlane (used by the parent proof whenever it writes q^-1 y = graphPoint(a(y), b(y)) and P y = q(graphPoint(a(y), 0))).

Notation. For a in R^n and b in R^l, graphPoint a b is the vector of R^(n+l) whose coordinate with index castAdd l i (i < n) is a_i and whose coordinate with index natAdd n j (j < l) is b_j (definition via Fin.append). Every index k in Fin (n+l) is of exactly one of these two forms (Fin.addCases). e_k is the k-th standard basis vector. H := horizontalPlane n l = span{e_(castAdd l i) : i < n}, T_0 := rotatedPlane q = q(H) (Submodule.map), and P is the orthogonal projection onto T_0 (starProjection).

1. (i) Both sides are vectors of R^(n+l); compare coordinates. Subtraction in EuclideanSpace is coordinatewise. At an index castAdd l i both sides equal a_i - a'_i, and at an index natAdd n j both sides equal b_j - b'_j (Fin.append_left, Fin.append_right). Hence graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b' = graphPoint (a - a') (b - b').
2. (ii) For z in EuclideanSpace, |z|^2 = sum_k z_k^2. Split the sum over Fin (n+l) into the castAdd part and the natAdd part (Fin.sum_univ_add). For z = graphPoint a b this gives sum_i a_i^2 + sum_j b_j^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2.
3. (iii) Given z, put a := (z_(castAdd l i))_(i<n) in R^n and b := (z_(natAdd n j))_(j<l) in R^l. By the coordinate description of step 1, graphPoint a b and z have the same coordinates at every index, so z = graphPoint a b.
4. (iv) First, graphPoint a 0 = sum_i a_i e_(castAdd l i) (compare coordinates), so graphPoint a 0 lies in H and u := q(graphPoint a 0) lies in T_0 = q(H).
5. All castAdd-coordinates of graphPoint 0 b vanish, so <graphPoint 0 b, e_(castAdd l i)> = 0 for every i, hence (by linearity in the second argument) <graphPoint 0 b, h> = 0 for every h in H.
6. A linear isometry preserves inner products (polarization identity), so for every v = q(h) in T_0 we get <q(graphPoint 0 b), v> = <graphPoint 0 b, h> = 0. Thus w := q(graphPoint 0 b) lies in the orthogonal complement of T_0.

subproblems.title: Smooth radial cutoff with ζ = 1 on B_{ρ/2}(ξ), ζ = 0 off B°_ρ(ξ), and |Dζ| <= 3/ρ
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (ξ : Rn m) (ρ : ℝ), 0 < ρ → ∃ ζ : Rn m → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ζ ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ ζ x ∧ ζ x ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ x ∈ Metric.closedBall ξ (ρ / 2), ζ x = 1) ∧ (∀ x, ρ ≤ dist x ξ → ζ x = 0) ∧ ∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ ζ x‖ ≤ 3 / ρ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Context. This child supplies the cutoff h_c of step 3 of the parent proof. gwe_vfv_localized_first_variation applies it with m = n + l, xi = 0 and rho = 2r, so that h_c = 1 on B_r(0) and h_c = 0 where |y| >= 2r. The parent instance r = 5 sigma/16 gives rho = 5 sigma/8, as in the supplied proof. It is the comparator-accepted declaration of DAG node root.tilt_excess_height_estimate-a1.smooth_cutoff-a1 (candidate commit cfec068), already a resolved dependency of this node. It is reused with its identical frozen Lean type, title, statement and empty dependency list; the proof below is the accepted argument formalized there.

Source (as recorded for the accepted node; 'the parent' and 'the supplied proof' in the rest of this text refer to that node's own parent, not to gwe_vertical_first_variation): the cutoff in step 2 of the supplied proof (Simon 5.2.1 proof: "ζ ≡ 1 in B_{ρ/2}, ζ ≡ 0 outside B_ρ, |∇ζ| <= 3/ρ"), constructed explicitly. In Lean, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) means C^infinity.

Let S := Real.smoothTransition. Mathlib (Analysis/SpecialFunctions/SmoothTransition.lean) gives:
- S is C^infinity (Real.smoothTransition.contDiff);
- 0 <= S <= 1 (nonneg, le_one);
- S(s) = 0 for s <= 0 (zero_of_nonpos);
- S(s) = 1 for s >= 1 (one_of_one_le).

1. The bump g. Define g(t) := S(12(t − 1/2)) · S(12(1 − t)) for t ∈ R.
  - g is C^infinity, as a product of compositions of C^infinity maps with affine maps.
  - 0 <= g <= 1.
  - g(t) = 0 for t <= 1/2 (first factor) and for t >= 1 (second factor).
  - g(t) = 1 for 7/12 <= t <= 11/12, where both arguments are >= 1.

2. The normalizing constant. Let c := ∫_{1/2}^{1} g(s) ds. Since g >= 0 on [1/2, 1] and g = 1 on [7/12, 11/12] ⊆ [1/2, 1], monotonicity of the integral gives c >= ∫_{7/12}^{11/12} 1 ds = 1/3 > 0. (In fact c = 5/12 by the symmetry S(s) + S(1 − s) = 1, but only c >= 1/3 is used.)

3. The profile φ. Define φ(t) := 1 − c^{-1} ∫_{1/2}^{t} g(s) ds (oriented interval integral).
  - g is continuous, so the fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_hasDerivAt_right) shows φ is differentiable everywhere with φ'(t) = −c^{-1} g(t).
  - φ' = −c^{-1} g is C^infinity, so φ is C^infinity (contDiff_infty_iff_deriv).
  - |φ'(t)| = c^{-1} g(t) <= c^{-1} <= 3 for all t, so φ is 3-Lipschitz by the mean value theorem.

4. Values of φ.
  - If t <= 1/2: g = 0 on [t, 1/2], so ∫_{1/2}^{t} g = −∫_{t}^{1/2} g = 0 and φ(t) = 1.
  - If t >= 1: ∫_{1/2}^{t} g = ∫_{1/2}^{1} g + ∫_{1}^{t} g = c + 0, so φ(t) = 0.
  - If 1/2 <= t <= 1: g >= 0 gives 0 <= ∫_{1/2}^{t} g <= ∫_{1/2}^{1} g = c, so 0 <= φ(t) <= 1.
  Hence 0 <= φ <= 1 on R.

5. The cutoff. Given m, ξ ∈ R^m and ρ > 0, define ζ(x) := φ(‖x − ξ‖/ρ). By step 4:
  - 0 <= ζ <= 1;
  - if x ∈ closedBall ξ (ρ/2), then ‖x − ξ‖/ρ <= 1/2 and ζ(x) = 1;
  - if dist(x, ξ) = ‖x − ξ‖ >= ρ, then ‖x − ξ‖/ρ >= 1 and ζ(x) = 0.

6. Smoothness. Let x ∈ R^m.
  - Case A, ‖x − ξ‖ < ρ/2: the open ball B°_{ρ/2}(ξ) is a neighbourhood of x on which ζ ≡ 1 (step 5). So ζ agrees with a constant near x, ζ is C^infinity at x, and Dζ(x) = 0.
  - Case B, x ≠ ξ: y ↦ ‖y − ξ‖ is C^infinity near x, since the Euclidean norm is C^infinity away from 0 (contDiffAt_norm, composed with y ↦ y − ξ). So ζ = φ ∘ (y ↦ ‖y − ξ‖/ρ) is C^infinity at x.
  Every x falls in case A or case B (x = ξ is in case A). So ζ is C^infinity at every point, i.e. ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ζ (contDiff_iff_contDiffAt).

7. The gradient bound. ζ is (3/ρ)-Lipschitz on R^m, because φ is 3-Lipschitz and the norm is 1-Lipschitz:
    |ζ(x) − ζ(y)| <= 3 · |‖x − ξ‖/ρ − ‖y − ξ‖/ρ| <= (3/ρ) ‖x − y‖.
  A K-Lipschitz function has ‖Dζ(x)‖ <= K at every point (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz). Hence ‖fderiv ℝ ζ x‖ <= 3/ρ for every x.
  Equivalently, by the chain rule in case B, Dζ(x)v = φ'(‖x − ξ‖/ρ) ρ^{-1} ⟨(x − ξ)/‖x − ξ‖, v⟩, so ‖Dζ(x)‖ = |φ'(‖x − ξ‖/ρ)|/ρ <= 3/ρ; and Dζ(x) = 0 in case A. ∎
proof_key_steps: g(t) = S(12(t−1/2))·S(12(1−t)) with S = Real.smoothTransition: C^∞, 0 <= g <= 1, zero off (1/2,1), equal to 1 on [7/12,11/12]
ζ(x) = φ(‖x−ξ‖/ρ): ζ = 1 on closedBall ξ (ρ/2), ζ = 0 when dist x ξ >= ρ
ζ is C^∞: locally constant near ξ, and a composition with the smooth norm away from ξ
ζ is (3/ρ)-Lipschitz, hence ‖fderiv ℝ ζ x‖ <= 3/ρ

subproblems.title: Sup bound from a gradient bound: |ζ| <= M r when tsupport ζ ⊆ B°_r(0)
subproblems.statement: Let n >= 1, let ζ : R^n → R be differentiable, let r >= 0 with tsupport ζ contained in the open ball B°_r(0), and let M be a real number with ‖∇ζ(x)‖ <= M for every x ∈ R^n (∇ζ = gradient ζ). Then |ζ(y)| <= M r for every y ∈ R^n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ (ζ : Rn n → ℝ) (r M : ℝ), 0 ≤ r → Differentiable ℝ ζ → tsupport ζ ⊆ ball 0 r → (∀ x, ‖gradient ζ x‖ ≤ M) → ∀ y, |ζ y| ≤ M * r
subproblems.natural_proof:
Context. This is step 1(v) of the parent proof: the bound |ζ(a(x))| <= M σ/4 used for the curvature term in step 7. Here it is stated for a general radius r >= 0 and a differentiable ζ. The parent applies it with r = σ/4, using tsupport ζ ⊆ B°_{σ/4}(0) and Differentiable ℝ ζ (from ContDiff ℝ 1 ζ).

1. M >= 0, since M >= ‖∇ζ(0)‖ >= 0.
2. ζ vanishes off the open ball: if ‖z‖ >= r then ζ(z) = 0. Indeed, if ζ(z) ≠ 0 then z ∈ support ζ ⊆ tsupport ζ ⊆ B°_r(0) (subset_tsupport), i.e. ‖z‖ < r, a contradiction.
3. ‖Dζ(x)‖ <= M for every x. By definition ∇ζ(x) = (toDual ℝ R^n)^{-1}(Dζ(x)), and the Riesz map toDual is a linear isometry equivalence. So ‖∇ζ(x)‖ = ‖Dζ(x)‖ (LinearIsometryEquiv.norm_map).
4. Case ‖y‖ >= r. By step 2, ζ(y) = 0, so |ζ(y)| = 0 <= M r, because M >= 0 (step 1) and r >= 0.
5. Case ‖y‖ < r. Choose a unit vector w with ‖y − r w‖ <= r.
   - If y = 0, take w := EuclideanSpace.single ⟨0, _⟩ 1, the first standard basis vector; it exists because n >= 1. Then ‖w‖ = 1 and ‖y − r w‖ = ‖r w‖ = r.
   - If y ≠ 0, take w := ‖y‖^{-1} y, so ‖w‖ = 1. Then y − r w = (1 − r ‖y‖^{-1}) y. Since 0 < ‖y‖ < r, we have 1 − r ‖y‖^{-1} <= 0. Hence ‖y − r w‖ = (r ‖y‖^{-1} − 1) ‖y‖ = r − ‖y‖ <= r.
6. ‖r w‖ = r ‖w‖ = r (as r >= 0), so ζ(r w) = 0 by step 2.
7. Apply the mean value inequality on the convex set R^n (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le with s = univ and C = M). ζ is differentiable at every point, and ‖Dζ‖ <= M by step 3. So |ζ(y) − ζ(r w)| <= M ‖y − r w‖.
8. By steps 5-7 and M >= 0: |ζ(y)| = |ζ(y) − ζ(r w)| <= M ‖y − r w‖ <= M r. ∎
proof_key_steps: M >= ‖∇ζ(0)‖ >= 0, and ‖Dζ(x)‖ = ‖∇ζ(x)‖ <= M (the Riesz map is an isometry)
ζ(z) = 0 whenever ‖z‖ >= r, because tsupport ζ ⊆ B°_r(0)
for ‖y‖ < r pick a unit vector w with ‖y − r w‖ <= r: w = y/‖y‖, or a standard basis vector if y = 0 (needs n >= 1)
mean value inequality: |ζ(y)| = |ζ(y) − ζ(r w)| <= M ‖y − r w‖ <= M r

subproblems.title: Height localization in rotated coordinates: ‖x‖ <= ‖a(x)‖ + dist(x, q(R^n × {0}))
subproblems.statement: For all n, l ∈ N, every linear isometry q of R^{n+l} and every x ∈ R^{n+l}: ‖x‖ <= ‖a(x)‖ + dist(x, T). Here a(x) := (EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd (q^{-1} x)).1 ∈ R^n is the first block of q^{-1} x, with the Euclidean norm of R^n, and T = rotatedPlane q = q(R^n × {0}). The distance is Metric.infDist to the subspace T.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (x : Amb n ℓ), ‖x‖ ≤ ‖(EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd (q.symm x)).1‖ + infDist x (rotatedPlane q : Set (Amb n ℓ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Context. This is the geometric core of step 2 of the parent proof (Simon 4.5 (5)). In the parent, ‖a(x)‖ < σ/4 (because a(x) ∈ tsupport ζ ⊆ B°_{σ/4}(0)) and dist(x, T) <= σ/16 (the height hypothesis); this lemma then gives ‖x‖ < 5σ/16. It uses lip_approx_graph_coordinates (GC), parts (i)-(iv), and hsNorm_starProjection_trace_identities (PA), part (ii). PA is applied with m = n + l, since Amb n l is by definition Rn (n + l).

1. By GC(iii) there are a ∈ R^n and b ∈ R^l with q^{-1} x = graphPoint a b.
2. a(x) = a. For i < n, the i-th coordinate of (finAddEquivProd z).1 is z_{castAdd l i}. The castAdd coordinates of graphPoint a b are those of a (graphPoint is defined via Fin.append; Fin.append_left). Compare coordinates.
3. x = q(q^{-1} x) = q(graphPoint a b).
4. Let P = p_T be the orthogonal projection onto T, and p_{T⊥} = 1 − P the projection onto T⊥ (Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal'). By GC(iv), P x = q(graphPoint a 0). Since q is linear, GC(i) gives
   p_{T⊥} x = q(graphPoint a b) − q(graphPoint a 0) = q(graphPoint a b − graphPoint a 0) = q(graphPoint (a − a) (b − 0)) = q(graphPoint 0 b).
5. By GC(ii), ‖graphPoint 0 b‖^2 = ‖0‖^2 + ‖b‖^2 = ‖b‖^2. Both norms are nonnegative, so ‖graphPoint 0 b‖ = ‖b‖.
6. By PA(ii), dist(x, T) = ‖p_{T⊥} x‖ = ‖q(graphPoint 0 b)‖ = ‖graphPoint 0 b‖ = ‖b‖, using that q is an isometry and step 5.
7. By step 3, the isometry property of q and GC(ii): ‖x‖^2 = ‖graphPoint a b‖^2 = ‖a‖^2 + ‖b‖^2 <= (‖a‖ + ‖b‖)^2.
8. Since ‖x‖ >= 0 and ‖a‖ + ‖b‖ >= 0, step 7 gives ‖x‖ <= ‖a‖ + ‖b‖ = ‖a(x)‖ + dist(x, T), by steps 2 and 6. ∎
proof_key_steps: q^{-1} x = graphPoint a b with a = a(x) (GC(iii) and the castAdd coordinates)
p_{T⊥} x = x − p_T x = q(graphPoint 0 b) (GC(iv), GC(i))
dist(x, T) = ‖p_{T⊥} x‖ = ‖b‖ (PA(ii), q an isometry, GC(ii))

subproblems.title: Chain rule in rotated coordinates: D(ζ ∘ a)(x) = ⟨q(graphPoint (∇ζ(a(x))) 0), ·⟩
subproblems.statement: Let n, l ∈ N, let q be a linear isometry of R^{n+l}, ζ : R^n → R and x ∈ R^{n+l}. Write a(y) := (EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd (q^{-1} y)).1 ∈ R^n, and assume ζ is differentiable at a(x). Then y ↦ ζ(a(y)) has Fréchet derivative at x equal to the continuous linear functional v ↦ ⟨q(graphPoint (∇ζ(a(x))) 0), v⟩ (innerSL ℝ of that vector; ∇ = gradient).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (ζ : Rn n → ℝ) (x : Amb n ℓ), DifferentiableAt ℝ ζ (EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd (q.symm x)).1 → HasFDerivAt (fun y : Amb n ℓ => ζ (EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd (q.symm y)).1) (innerSL ℝ (q (graphPoint (gradient ζ (EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd (q.symm x)).1) 0))) x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Context. This is step 1(ii) of the parent proof: D ζ~(x) v = ⟨g(x), v⟩, with ζ~ = ζ ∘ a and g(x) = q(graphPoint (∇ζ(a(x))) 0). (The C^1 regularity of ζ~ in step 1(i) is a one-line ContDiff.comp in the parent.) The parent combines it with gwe_vfv_divM_smul_const_eq_inner to identify div_M(ζ~ e'_j) with the parent's integrand.

1. a is a continuous linear map. Indeed a = L := fst ∘ finAddEquivProd ∘ q^{-1}. Here finAddEquivProd : R^{n+l} ≃L[ℝ] R^n × R^l is a continuous linear equivalence, q^{-1} is a linear isometry equivalence, and fst is the continuous linear first projection. L y = (finAddEquivProd (q^{-1} y)).1 holds by definition, so y ↦ ζ(a(y)) is ζ ∘ L.
2. Chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp with ContinuousLinearMap.hasFDerivAt; ζ is differentiable at L x): ζ ∘ L has Fréchet derivative Dζ(a(x)) ∘ L at x.
3. Coordinate identity: for w ∈ R^n and z ∈ R^{n+l}, ⟨graphPoint w 0, z⟩ = ⟨w, (finAddEquivProd z).1⟩.
   - The inner product on EuclideanSpace is Σ_k u_k z_k (PiLp.inner_apply). Split the sum over Fin (n + l) into its castAdd and natAdd parts (Fin.sum_univ_add).
   - graphPoint w 0 has castAdd coordinates w_i and natAdd coordinates 0 (Fin.append_left, Fin.append_right), and (finAddEquivProd z).1 has i-th coordinate z_{castAdd l i}.
   - So the sum is Σ_i w_i z_{castAdd l i} = ⟨w, (finAddEquivProd z).1⟩.
4. Let G := ∇ζ(a(x)) and v ∈ R^{n+l}. Then:
   - ⟨q(graphPoint G 0), v⟩ = ⟨graphPoint G 0, q^{-1} v⟩ (LinearIsometryEquiv.inner_map_eq_flip);
   - ⟨graphPoint G 0, q^{-1} v⟩ = ⟨G, a(v)⟩ (step 3 with z = q^{-1} v);
   - ⟨G, a(v)⟩ = Dζ(a(x))(a(v)), because by definition ∇ζ(p) = (toDual ℝ R^n)^{-1}(Dζ(p)) and ⟨(toDual)^{-1} φ, u⟩ = φ(u) (InnerProductSpace.toDual_symm_apply);
   - Dζ(a(x))(a(v)) = (Dζ(a(x)) ∘ L)(v).
5. By step 4, the continuous linear maps innerSL ℝ (q(graphPoint G 0)) and Dζ(a(x)) ∘ L agree at every v, hence are equal. Step 2 then gives the claim (HasFDerivAt.congr_fderiv). ∎
proof_key_steps: a = fst ∘ finAddEquivProd ∘ q^{-1} is continuous linear, so the chain rule gives D(ζ ∘ a)(x) = Dζ(a(x)) ∘ a
⟨graphPoint w 0, z⟩ = ⟨w, (finAddEquivProd z).1⟩ (split the coordinate sum with Fin.sum_univ_add)
⟨q(graphPoint G 0), v⟩ = ⟨graphPoint G 0, q^{-1} v⟩ = ⟨G, a(v)⟩ = Dζ(a(x))(a(v)) (q an isometry; definition of the gradient)

subproblems.title: Tangential divergence of a rank-one field: div_M(f e)(x) = ⟨p_x e, p_x g⟩ when Df(x) = ⟨g, ·⟩
subproblems.statement: Let n, l ∈ N, U ⊆ R^{n+l}, and V a rectifiable n-varifold in U with tangent projection p_x = V.tangentProj x. Let f : R^{n+l} → R and e, g, x ∈ R^{n+l}, and assume f has Fréchet derivative v ↦ ⟨g, v⟩ at x. Then the tangential divergence of the field y ↦ f(y) e at x satisfies V.divM (y ↦ f(y) e) x = ⟨p_x e, p_x g⟩.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (f : Amb n ℓ → ℝ) (e g x : Amb n ℓ), HasFDerivAt f (innerSL ℝ g) x → V.divM (fun y => f y • e) x = inner ℝ (V.tangentProj x e) (V.tangentProj x g)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Context. This is the trace computation of step 5, Case B, of the parent proof: trace(v ↦ ⟨g, p_x v⟩ e) = ⟨g, p_x e⟩ = ⟨p_x e, p_x g⟩, because p_x is self-adjoint and idempotent. The parent applies it at every x, with f = ζ ∘ a, e = e'_j and g = g(x); the derivative comes from gwe_vfv_hasFDerivAt_comp_first_block.

1. Write p := V.tangentProj x. Claim: ⟨p u, p v⟩ = ⟨u, p v⟩ for all u, v. By definition, p is either K.starProjection for some subspace K (the orthogonal projection onto the approximate tangent space chosen by Classical.choose), or 0.
   - If p = K.starProjection: ⟨p u, p v⟩ = ⟨u, p(p v)⟩ by self-adjointness (Submodule.inner_starProjection_left_eq_right). Also p(p v) = p v, because p v ∈ K (Submodule.starProjection_apply_mem, Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff).
   - If p = 0, both sides are 0.
2. The field X(y) := f(y) e has Fréchet derivative D X(x) = (innerSL ℝ g).smulRight e, i.e. v ↦ ⟨g, v⟩ e (HasFDerivAt.smul_const). Hence fderiv ℝ X x is this map.
3. By definition V.divM X x = trace(D X(x) ∘ p). The composition is w ↦ ⟨g, p w⟩ e, i.e. ψ.smulRight e for the linear functional ψ := ⟨g, p ·⟩ = (innerSL ℝ g) ∘ p (check pointwise).
4. On the finite-dimensional free module R^{n+l}, the trace of the rank-one map w ↦ ψ(w) e is ψ(e) (LinearMap.trace_smulRight). So V.divM X x = ⟨g, p e⟩.
5. By step 1 with u = g and v = e, ⟨g, p e⟩ = ⟨p g, p e⟩, which equals ⟨p e, p g⟩ by symmetry of the real inner product (real_inner_comm). ∎
proof_key_steps: p_x is an orthogonal projection or 0, so ⟨p u, p v⟩ = ⟨u, p v⟩
D(f e)(x) = ⟨g, ·⟩ e (HasFDerivAt.smul_const)
D(f e)(x) ∘ p = (⟨g, p ·⟩).smulRight e, whose trace is ⟨g, p e⟩ (LinearMap.trace_smulRight)
⟨g, p e⟩ = ⟨p g, p e⟩ = ⟨p e, p g⟩

subproblems.title: The weight of a rectifiable varifold is concentrated on its support (Simon 4.5, proof step (1a))
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U an arbitrary subset of R^{n+l} = EuclideanSpace R (Fin (n+l)), and V a contract rectifiable n-varifold in U (structure RectifiableVarifold n l U). V has carrier M, so M ⊆ U and M is H^n-null-measurable (H^n = μHE[n]), and multiplicity θ. Its weight is μ = V.weight = (H^n restricted to M) with density x ↦ ofReal(θ(x)), and its support is spt V = V.support = U ∩ supp μ, where supp μ = μ.support is the support of the measure μ. Then μ-almost every point of R^{n+l} lies in spt V, i.e. μ(R^{n+l} \ spt V) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U), ∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, x ∈ V.support
subproblems.natural_proof:
Context. This child supplies the first bullet of step 6 of the parent proof: mu-a.e. x lies in spt V = U cap supp mu. gwe_vfv_localized_first_variation uses it to pass from the pointwise identities on spt V to equality of integrals. It is the comparator-accepted declaration of DAG node root.tilt_excess_decay-a1.decay_at_origin-a1.graph_height_excess-a1.ae_mem_support-a1 (candidate commit 8c1c608). It is reused with its identical frozen Lean type, title, statement and empty dependency list; the proof below is the accepted argument formalized there.

Source (as recorded for the accepted node; 'the parent' and 'the supplied proof' in the rest of this text refer to that node's own parent, not to gwe_vertical_first_variation): step (1a) of the parent proof, stated for an arbitrary contract rectifiable varifold. The parent uses it in its step 4, for the part of B̄_r(τ) off the graph.

Notation.
- ν := μHE[n].restrict M, the Hausdorff measure H^n restricted to the carrier M.
- ρ(x) := ENNReal.ofReal(θ(x)).
- μ := V.weight = ν.withDensity ρ, by the definition of RectifiableVarifold.weight.
- V.support = U ∩ μ.support, by the definition of RectifiableVarifold.support. Here μ.support is the set of points x every neighbourhood of which has positive μ-measure.

1. μ-a.e. point lies in μ.support. The ambient space R^{n+l} = EuclideanSpace R (Fin (n+l)) is second countable, hence hereditarily Lindelöf. The complement of μ.support is open, and every point of it has an open neighbourhood of μ-measure zero. By the Lindelöf property, countably many of these neighbourhoods cover the complement, so μ((μ.support)^c) = 0 by countable subadditivity. subproblems.title: Localized first variation for a field φ e with constant e: ∫_{B_s} div_M(φ e) dμ = −∫_{B_s} φ ⟨e, H⟩ dμ
subproblems.statement: Let n, l ∈ N, U ⊆ R^{n+l}, and V a rectifiable n-varifold in U with generalized mean curvature H in U; μ = V.weight. Let φ : R^{n+l} → R be C^1, let e ∈ R^{n+l}, and let r, s, R be real numbers with 0 < r, 2r <= R, r <= s <= R and B_R(0) ⊆ U (closed balls). Assume every x ∈ spt V ∩ B_R(0) with x ∈ tsupport φ satisfies ‖x‖ < r, where spt V = V.support = U ∩ supp μ. Then ∫_{B_s(0)} div_M(φ e) dμ = −∫_{B_s(0)} φ(x) ⟨e, H(x)⟩ dμ, where div_M(φ e)(x) = V.divM (y ↦ φ(y) e) x. These are Bochner integrals and no integrability is assumed; by Lean's convention a non-integrable integrand has integral 0.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Context. This is steps 3-6 of the parent proof (Simon 4.5 (6)), for a general C^1 function φ and vector e. The parent applies it with φ = ζ ∘ a, where a(y) = (finAddEquivProd (q^{-1} y)).1, and with e = e'_j, r = 5σ/16, s = σ/2, R = σ. The support hypothesis is the localization of step 2 (gwe_vfv_norm_le_first_block_add_infDist with the height hypothesis). This child uses exists_smooth_cutoff_half_ball_grad_le (CUT) and tdo_ghe_ae_mem_support.

1. Cutoff. Apply CUT with m = n + l, ξ = 0 and ρ = 2r > 0. It gives a C^∞ function χ : R^{n+l} → R with χ = 1 on closedBall 0 (2r/2) = B_r(0), and χ(y) = 0 whenever 2r <= dist(y, 0) = ‖y‖.
2. Test field. Let X(y) := (χ(y) φ(y)) e. X is C^1: χ is C^∞, hence C^1 (ContDiff.of_le), φ is C^1, and products and scalar multiples of a constant vector preserve C^1 (ContDiff.mul, ContDiff.smul with contDiff_const).
3. Support.
   - If X(y) ≠ 0 then χ(y) ≠ 0, so ‖y‖ < 2r by step 1. Hence support X ⊆ closedBall 0 (2r).
   - The closed ball is closed, so tsupport X ⊆ closedBall 0 (2r) (closure_minimal).
   - The closed ball is compact, so X has compact support (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset).
   - Since 2r <= R, tsupport X ⊆ closedBall 0 (2r) ⊆ closedBall 0 R ⊆ U.
4. First variation. Apply the second component of V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H to X: ∫ div_M X dμ = −∫ ⟨X(x), H(x)⟩ dμ.
5. Locality of the divergence. If Y = Z on a neighbourhood of x, then fderiv Y x = fderiv Z x (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq). Since V.divM Y x = trace(D Y(x) ∘ p_x) depends only on D Y(x), we get V.divM Y x = V.divM Z x. In particular, if Y = 0 near x then V.divM Y x = trace(0) = 0.
6. Pointwise identities. Let x ∈ spt V. Claim:
   (a) V.divM X x = 1_{B_s(0)}(x) · V.divM (φ e) x;
   (b) ⟨X(x), H(x)⟩ = 1_{B_s(0)}(x) · φ(x) ⟨e, H(x)⟩.
   Case 1: ‖x‖ < r.
   - The open ball B°_r(0) is a neighbourhood of x on which χ = 1 (step 1). So X = φ e near x, and V.divM X x = V.divM (φ e) x by step 5.
   - χ(x) = 1, so ⟨X(x), H(x)⟩ = ⟨φ(x) e, H(x)⟩ = φ(x) ⟨e, H(x)⟩.
   - Since ‖x‖ < r <= s, x ∈ B_s(0) and the indicator is 1.
   Case 2: r <= ‖x‖ <= R.
   - Then x ∈ spt V ∩ B_R(0) and ‖x‖ is not < r, so x ∉ tsupport φ by hypothesis.
   - Hence φ = 0 on a neighbourhood of x (notMem_tsupport_iff_eventuallyEq). So X = 0 and φ e = 0 near x, and both divergences vanish (step 5).
   - Also φ(x) = 0, so X(x) = 0 and φ(x) ⟨e, H(x)⟩ = 0. Both sides of (a) and (b) are 0, whatever the indicator.
   Case 3: ‖x‖ > R.
   - The set {y : ‖y‖ > R} is open and contains x. On it ‖y‖ > R >= 2r, so χ = 0 there (step 1).
   - Thus X = 0 near x, V.divM X x = 0 (step 5), and X(x) = 0.
   - Since ‖x‖ > R >= s, x ∉ B_s(0), so both right-hand sides are 0.
7. Almost everywhere. By tdo_ghe_ae_mem_support, μ-a.e. x lies in spt V. So (a) and (b) hold μ-a.e.
8. Integrals. The closed ball B_s(0) is measurable, so ∫_{B_s(0)} F dμ = ∫ 1_{B_s(0)} F dμ for every F (integral_indicator). Use integral_congr_ae, which needs no integrability, with step 7, and the identity of step 4:
   ∫_{B_s(0)} div_M(φ e) dμ = ∫ 1_{B_s(0)} div_M(φ e) dμ = ∫ div_M X dμ = −∫ ⟨X, H⟩ dμ = −∫ 1_{B_s(0)} φ ⟨e, H⟩ dμ = −∫_{B_s(0)} φ ⟨e, H⟩ dμ. ∎
